history.summary: Nikle (Nikla) Mahadev Mandir is Raigarh city's well-known Shiva temple, about 0.21 km from Raigarh railway station on the bank of a city lake that is now a popular walking spot. It is famous locally for its self-manifested (svayambhu) Shivling - 'Nikla Mahadev' - described in a Hindi travel video as having emerged from the earth itself ('swayam dharti se prakat'). One reviewer describes the temple as 200+ years old, but no founding inscription or dynastic attribution is documented online, so the age is reviewer-reported, not verified. The premises also house shrines of Swami Jagannath and Hanuman plus a park. AMBIGUITY: a second, distinct 'Nikle Mahadev Mandir' place listing exists at Kharsia (~32 km from Raigarh); this file documents the Raigarh-city temple corroborated by the yappe page and the temple's own business.site page.

name: Nikle Mahadev Mandir
town_description: Raigarh is an industrial city in northern Chhattisgarh, a major coal and steel hub on the Howrah-Mumbai rail line. It is also known for its Kathak dance tradition and as a gateway to the Kelo river valley.

travel.airport: Swami Vivekananda Airport, Raipur (~230 km) is the nearest major airport; Bilaspur (~130 km) has limited services
travel.railway: Raigarh railway station, about 0.21 km from the temple (on the Howrah-Mumbai main line)
travel.road: NH 49 and NH 153 connect Raigarh to Raipur and Sambalpur

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri draws large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented; Shiva temples are typically open from early morning to evening
